answer.evidence: In radon/visitors.py, ComplexityVisitor takes a no_assert flag (default False) in __init__ at line 157 and stores it at line 165. visit_Assert (around lines 257-260) does `self.complexity += not self.no_assert`. The boolean converts to 0 or 1, so an assert adds one branch only when assertion counting is enabled. The flag is passed on to nested visitors at line 279 (ComplexityVisitor(off=False, no_assert=self.no_assert)) and line 313 (class and method visitors). Review should check that every nested path keeps the flag, and that the comment at line 235 ("Ifs, with and assert statements count all as 1") still matches the conditional behavior. radon/complexity.py is the caller that builds the visitor and should be checked to confirm the option reaches it. radon/raw.py and radon/metrics.py have no assert-scoring logic and need only a brief check. Tests in radon/tests/test_complexity_utils.py cover the no_assert default, but I found no direct test that an assert adds 0 when the flag is set, so I recommend adding one.
